title: Derive an SDDC LCM component-upgrade contract from the VCF 9.1 specification and survive a mid-run access-token expiry
prompt:
Build a standard-library-only Python package that drives the VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC LCM component upgrade workflow against an SDDC/Fleet component. Applying an upgrade is asynchronous: the service accepts the request and returns a `Task`, and the upgrade is not done until that task reaches a terminal state. Upgrades also run long enough that the access token presented at the start of the run expires before the task finishes. When a request returns HTTP 401, obtain a fresh token, replay only that request, and continue. Do not restart the upgrade or lose the task already being polled.

Research and derive the wire contract from `specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml` at commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer. Write `docs/contract.json` naming the exact operationIds `getHealth`, `resolveDepotComponents`, `performComponentAction`, `getTask`, and `retryTask`, together with their methods, path templates, path/query/header parameters, request-body schemas, and the `TaskStatus` enum. Preserve two specification details: `getHealth` overrides the document-wide bearer-token security requirement with an empty one, and `retryTask` is keyed under `paths:` by a template that already carries its `?action=retry` query string. Record provenance in `docs/official_sources.json`: the repository, SPDX license, spec path, commit SHA, Git blob SHA, SHA-256 of the bytes fetched, and every operationId used.

Then implement `src/vcf_lcm/contract.py` and `src/vcf_lcm/client.py` against that contract. The client must build every request target from the contract rather than string literals, obtain its token lazily from a caller-supplied `token_provider`, refresh once and replay on HTTP 401, send no `Authorization` header on the unauthenticated operation, poll each task to a terminal state instead of assuming HTTP 202 means completion, and omit every optional field the caller left unset rather than sending it null, empty, or `{}`. `README.md` specifies the exact contract shape and remaining wire behavior.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. Verification checks the exact wire shape, token refresh and replay, polling continuity, unauthenticated health request, and optional-field omission. Do not modify `tests/`.
network_rationale: the agent must retrieve the OpenAPI specification from github.com to derive the contract and to compute the content digests recorded in docs/official_sources.json; verification itself is loopback-only
scenario: a component upgrade is applied against a Fleet depot, and the access token expires after the third successful authenticated request -- part way through polling the accepted task; the run must refresh the token, replay only the rejected read, and finish the same task, while sibling components exercise a task that ends FAILED and is resumed with retryTask, and a task that never leaves RUNNING
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves the upgrade was started exactly once across the token refresh, that polling resumed on the same task id, that the unauthenticated health operation carried no bearer token, and that every unset optional field was omitted rather than sent empty
